name: Lakhota
note: Lakhota retains the requested spelling for Lakota. This Exploration interpretation emphasizes eighteenth-century Plains communities, not a single timeless Sioux state. Settlement labels are geographic camp regions, not eight urban capitals. Mounted donor models and Inca building assets are visual approximations, not authentic Lakota armor or architecture. Personal-name pools include documented later people and are not an Exploration-period census.
intro: Across the grasslands, households carry the warmth of their hearths toward another season's gathering. Bison sustain the camp, skilled hands prepare hides, and riders follow paths between waters and wooded hills. Share the work of provision, renew the obligations of kin, and let the strength of your communities travel with the people.
overview: Lakhota communities join seasonal mobility, bison provisioning, skilled hidework, and relationships among camps. Shared resources support cultural life while riders and pathfinders protect movement across the Plains. Their history includes adaptation and changing homelands, rather than one fixed empire or a people confined to the past.

name: Navajo
note: The Navajo, or Dine, are distinct from Pueblo nations and other Athabaskan-speaking peoples. Exploration themes combine farming, household life, and post-contact pastoral and weaving developments. Labels are geographic homelands, not a centralized kingdom's cities. Native Inca assets and archer models are explicitly visual approximations. English labels avoid fabricated ceremonial terminology; personal-name pools include documented later names and modern surnames.
intro: Between sandstone walls, fields draw life from carefully tended soil and changing waters. Beyond the canyon, households gather their flocks, and patient hands turn wool into cloth. Sustain your neighbors through knowledge, craft, and exchange, and weave a future whose threads remain rooted in the land.
overview: Navajo households combine dryland cultivation, pastoral resources, textile skill, and regional exchange. Hogans and weaving places support communities spread across canyon and plateau landscapes. These changing practices belong to a living people, not an imagined uniform desert empire.

name: Zimbabwe
intro: Granite walls curve around households and courts on the southern plateau. Cattle graze beyond the stone, while gold moves toward distant ocean ports. Shape a realm whose prosperity rests on local skill and far-reaching exchange, and whose monuments speak in the language of patient masonry.
overview: Zimbabwe joins pastoral wealth, specialist stoneworking, and inland trade. Enclosures reward monumental ambition, while exchange courts connect resources to prosperous settlements. The kit spans related southern African traditions without treating every site as one dynasty's capital.
note: Great Zimbabwe and related Zimbabwe-culture settlements are the focus, not the modern republic. Mapungubwe is a predecessor; Khami and later sites represent successor traditions, and Manyikeni is a connected regional site. Indigenous African authorship is unequivocal; particular institutions remain reconstructed.

name: Byzantium
intro: At the meeting of seas, a Roman capital clothes old authority in silk and mosaic. Scholars copy, artisans weave, and mounted soldiers guard roads that join provinces to the court. Preserve learning through upheaval and give an enduring empire the means to renew itself.
overview: Byzantium rewards specialists, resource-rich cities, and cultural patronage. Imperial workshops support scholarship and diplomacy, while armored cavalry protects a connected urban core. Roman identity and institutional change matter more than an imagined unchanging medieval court.
note: Byzantium is the conventional modern label for the medieval Eastern Roman polity. City holdings shifted greatly over its history. Generic cavalry upgrades and basilica art are approximations, not reconstructed Byzantine models.

name: Ayutthaya
intro: Three rivers gather around an island crowned with towers. Rice barges, foreign merchants, and royal embassies pass beneath the gaze of monasteries. Open your markets without surrendering the court's authority, cultivate the floodplain, and make the waterways a meeting ground for the wider world.
overview: Ayutthaya turns river agriculture into commercial and cultural strength. Customs houses and monasteries complement productive fields, while connected cities sustain an outward-looking court. Tributary relationships and changing provincial control are not treated as fixed modern borders.
note: The kingdom of 1351–1767 is represented, not all Thai history. Mergui was held during particular periods; Sukhothai and southern centers entered changing subordinate relationships. Royal Spear Guard is descriptive, not a claimed archival regiment title.

name: Aztec
intro: Causeways cross bright water toward a city of temples and crowded markets. Gardens rise from shallow wetlands, feeding households and the ambitions of rulers. Bind allies and tributaries into your network, honor learning and craft, and reckon with the obligations that accompany imperial power.
overview: Aztec play combines intensive agriculture, commercial capacity, and strong infantry. Schools and markets support specialist cities, while tribute connections finance expansion. The Triple Alliance and its unequal relationships remain distinct from a single homogeneous national state.
note: Aztec denotes the Mexica-led Triple Alliance setting. Texcoco and Tlacopan were allies, not Mexica foundations; other labels include subordinate altepetl. Chinampas were fixed raised fields, not floating rafts. Native metal-armed donor art does not reproduce an obsidian-armed eagle warrior.

name: Mohawk
intro: Along the river valley, cultivated fields surround villages of bark-covered longhouses. Families share hearths, messengers carry words between communities, and councils weigh obligations beyond the palisade. Sustain the people of the Eastern Door through careful husbandry, reciprocal diplomacy, and the strength of relationships renewed.
overview: Mohawk communities thrive through shared households, productive fields, and connections between settlements. Defensive mobility protects village networks. Confederacy diplomacy is represented as a relationship among distinct nations, not as permission to relabel all Haudenosaunee traditions uniquely Mohawk.
note: Kanienkehaka is an unaccented rendering of Kanien'keha:ka. Labels include archaeological site names rather than invented Indigenous city names; they span successive occupations. Caughnawaga means the historical Mohawk Valley village here, not modern Kahnawake. Base-game Inca visual cultures are an asset-only approximation, not Mohawk architecture, dress, or ancestry. Bow Warrior's donor upgrades are gameplay abstractions, including later firearms.

name: Franks
intro: Roads lead from royal estates to a court that seldom stands still. In workshops and monasteries, hands provision armies and reshape the written word. Unite competing households, cultivate learning beside lordship, and give your far-flung realm institutions strong enough to travel with its rulers.
overview: Frankish royal estates provision expansion while monasteries cultivate scholarship. Connected households support mounted service and cultural patronage. Merovingian foundations and Carolingian reforms are distinguished from the later kingdoms and feudal stereotypes often projected backward upon them.
note: The focus spans Merovingian and Carolingian Frankish realms, not modern France alone. Missus Dominicus refers to an envoy, not an ecclesiastical rank. Pfalzkapelle is the established modern German name of Aachen's historical palace chapel; Fiscus and Palatium are attested medieval Latin institutional terms. Cavalry donors compress changing forms of military service rather than claim universal heavy knights under Clovis.

name: Seljuks
intro: Across upland pastures and stone-built cities, mounted households meet the world of the caravan. Sheltered courtyards welcome travelers, while scholars gather beneath monumental portals. Secure the roads, sustain the herds, and turn the movement of people and goods into a foundation for lasting rule.
overview: Seljuk play links pastoral military strength with protected commerce and scholarly endowments. Caravan infrastructure supports connected cities, while mounted troops keep their mobility. Great Seljuk and Anatolian Rum traditions are related but not conflated into one unchanging administration.
note: This composite uses Great Seljuk and Rum Seljuk history, with city labels explicitly spanning both. Mounted melee donors approximate mobile cavalry; they do not supply a native ranged horse-archer attack. Caravanserai donor is active Exploration content.

name: Rus
intro: Boats pass between forest rivers, their cargoes hauled across the land where waters divide. Princely courts gather merchants and retainers; new churches lift their roofs above timber walls. Connect distant settlements, negotiate rival claims, and make your river roads carry learning as well as wealth.
overview: Rus prospers through rivers, commercial connections, and princely patronage. Fortified centers support a durable infantry retinue while churches encourage cultural and scholarly growth. Its diverse medieval principalities are not equated with any single modern national state.
note: The focus is medieval Rus, particularly the Kyivan-era network and related principalities. Settlement labels use recognizable modern transliterations. It is not a Muscovite, Russian imperial, or exclusively Scandinavian civilization.

name: Lombards
intro: Within old Roman walls, new rulers establish courts, churches, and written law. Dukes guard their own ambitions even as royal foundations gather prestige. Reconcile local power with a wider realm, sustain the obligations of free households, and leave an enduring mark upon the cities of Italy.
overview: Lombard courts combine local military obligations with legal and monastic patronage. Connected ducal centers reward production and happiness, while cultural institutions preserve a distinctive Italian synthesis. Southern successor principalities extend the story beyond the northern kingdom's fall.
note: Lombards are the early medieval people and Italian polities, not later Lombard banking houses. Arimannus describes a free man associated with public and military obligations, not a universally standardized troop. Salerno represents the later southern Lombard principality.

name: Timurids
intro: Blue tile catches the sunlight above gardens and crowded workshops. From campaigns and migrations come the people whose hands remake imperial cities; at court, scholars measure the stars. Harness cavalry and patronage, but remember that the brilliance of monuments casts shadows upon the roads of conquest.
overview: Timurid cavalry supports an ambitious network of specialist cities, monumental building, and astronomical learning. Court workshops turn concentrated skill into culture. The kit acknowledges coerced artisan transfers and destructive conquest alongside the achievements of later scholarly patrons.
note: The Timurid dynasty of Central Asia and Iran is the focus, not the later Mughal Empire. Building ensembles are abstractions, not claims that every Registan monument is Timurid. Generic cavalry donors do not reproduce mounted archery.

name: Venice
intro: Tides rise beneath a city whose streets open onto the sea. Shipwrights, merchants, and pilots bind the lagoon to harbors far beyond the horizon. Guard your convoys, bargain for access, and build a republic whose wealth depends upon the fragile meeting of water, labor, and law.
overview: Venice specializes in coastal wealth, commercial capacity, and naval production. Waterfront workshops and trading houses reward maritime connections, while overseas settlements extend opportunity and risk. Republic, empire, and lagoon ecology remain inseparable parts of its history.
note: Venetian historical place names identify lagoon communities and overseas possessions, not ethnic or permanent claims. Native sailing-ship donors approximate the military role of a war galley; no new galley mesh is supplied.

name: Almohads
intro: From Atlas valleys, a reforming movement reaches the cities on both sides of the strait. Great mosques and enclosed gardens announce the ambitions of caliphs. Join water to cultivated land, gather the resources of many provinces, and confront the tensions between stern doctrine and a diverse empire.
overview: Almohad cities combine irrigated agriculture, monumental patronage, and territorial integration. Gardens and reservoirs support productive urban centers, while infantry anchors expansion. Their religious reform and coercive policies are acknowledged rather than replaced by a timeless image of Andalusian tolerance.
note: The Almohad movement and caliphate are distinct from the preceding Almoravids and later Marinids. Marrakesh was an inherited Almoravid foundation. Waterworks frequently reused earlier infrastructure; generic spear infantry is not a claimed formal corps.

name: Khwarazmians
intro: Canals divide the green oasis from the dry horizon, and caravan roads converge upon crowded markets. From the lower Oxus, rulers reach toward the cities of Iran and Transoxiana. Sustain the waterworks beneath imperial ambition, strengthen your horsemen, and keep prosperity moving between vulnerable centers.
overview: Khwarazmian power grows from river agriculture, caravan revenues, and mounted military households. Resource capacity and connected cities finance expansion. The Anushteginid empire's rapid growth and fragile cohesion are distinguished from the much longer cultural history of Khwarazm.
note: This kit centers on the Anushteginid Khwarazmshahs, especially the twelfth and early thirteenth centuries. Imperial city labels include brief conquests and changing allegiances. It does not claim the ninth-century scholar al-Khwarizmi served this later dynasty.

name: Papal States
intro: Pilgrims enter a city where sacred authority also bears the burdens of government. Chanceries issue letters, builders transform public spaces, and hired captains defend contested lands. Balance communes, noble families, and courtly ambition as patronage gives visible form to a territorial state.
overview: Papal States play combines administration, cultural commissions, and connections among territorial centers. Chanceries finance specialist cities while hired cavalry protects secular possessions. Papal religious leadership and the practical government of a changing Italian state are related but distinct.
note: This is the pre-1870 secular territorial polity, not Vatican City, established in 1929, or the worldwide Catholic Church. Avignon was a papal possession from 1348 and an earlier court seat. Famous Swiss Guard infantry are not mislabeled as condottieri.

name: Taíno
intro: Across warm channels, canoes carry visitors, news, and carefully made gifts. Around cultivated gardens and open plazas, households gather for work, ceremony, and remembered histories. Nurture relationships between distinct island communities, sustain the harvest, and let your people's voices endure beyond the violence of arriving empires.
overview: Taíno communities combine cassava cultivation, interisland exchange, and ceremonial gathering. Household prosperity supports cultural authority rather than mainland river administration. Diverse cacicazgos and surviving Indigenous identities remain central, without imagining a single Caribbean empire or an extinct people.
note: A separate Exploration identity, not internal Antiquity key TAINO, now The Orinoco. Labels mix Hispaniolan regional polities and archaeological ceremonial sites, not eight simultaneous capitals; Tibes represents an earlier ceremonial heritage, not an exclusively late Taíno foundation. Local terms use established unaccented spellings; poorly attested unit titles remain explicit English descriptions. Base-game Inca visual cultures are an asset-only approximation, not Caribbean architecture, dress, or ancestry. Caribbean models are not newly authored.
